scenario.brief: Dana leads an orders portal and wrote its login and admin code herself. Launch is in two weeks. She wants your plan for making authentication and access control safe.
scenario.role: Backend engineer asked to secure the auth module before launch.
scenario.goal: Find the security flaws, explain each risk, and propose a fix order and a role model.
rules: Dana is in the chat. She answers questions about the app, its users and her choices.
She will not hand you a list of problems. Ask, then judge.
Ask about anything: users, roles, the frontend, what is already live.
When you are ready, press End and debrief.
scenario.artifactNote: 50 lines, users held in memory. Every email and secret here is a made-up demo value.

levels: Not raised
Says the password hash is too weak or lacks a salt
Asks for a slow salted hash such as bcrypt, and a plan for the pilot accounts
Not raised
Notes the hard-coded secret or the missing expiry
Asks for an environment secret and a short expiry, and notes a stolen token cannot be revoked
Not raised
Says the cookie should be httpOnly
Asks for httpOnly, secure and sameSite, and has the frontend call /me instead of reading the token
Not raised
Notices /admin/users has no role check
Asks for a role check that answers 403, and for password hashes to leave the response
Not raised
Says the role should not come from the request body
Says the server sets role user, and admins are promoted through a separate, deliberate path
Not raised
Notes the two error messages differ or that the user record is returned
Asks for one generic 401 and a login response without the user record
Not raised
Mentions rate limiting or input validation
Asks for per-IP and per-account limits, plus validation that stops a missing-password crash
Not raised
Lists fixes without an order
Plans deny-by-default roles that can grow a support role, and fixes privilege escalation first
